title: React Dependencies & Styling the Keeper App
summary: Polishes the Keeper app by installing Material UI, swapping text buttons for icon components, using a Fab button with a Zoom transition, collapsing the create form until the textarea is clicked, and adding a patterned background. Closes by noting React alone does not persist data.

concepts.heading: Starting point and why to use the provided project
points: The styled demo has icons, an expanding note form, a hover effect on the add button and a patterned page background.

The supplied starter differs from the previous lesson: styles.css has new rules and the form in CreateArea carries className='create-note'. Without both, the Fab renders grey and misplaced. Copy the stylesheet and add the class if you continue your own copy.

(Extra) In the reference styles.css the form, input/textarea and button rules are written as form.create-note, form.create-note input/textarea and form.create-note button. The Fab renders a real <button> element, so form.create-note button is what makes it yellow, round and absolutely positioned at the bottom-right of the form.

concepts.heading: Installing Material UI
points: Material UI (MUI) is a library of pre-built React components following Google's Material Design, so appearance and some behaviour come ready-made.
The video uses two packages, core (components) and icons. Locally, install them with npm; in a CodeSandbox, use Add Dependency.
(Extra) Per the preceding note lecture, use current packages: npm install @mui/material @mui/icons-material @emotion/react @emotion/styled. The reference repo uses MUI v7 with React 19.
Advantage over Bootstrap or icon fonts: each component bundles its markup, styles and logic as JSX, so it behaves like any other component you write.

concepts.heading: Icons as components
points: Find an icon in the MUI icon search page, copy its import line, and render it as a self-closing component.
Note.jsx: import DeleteIcon and put <DeleteIcon /> inside the button instead of the word DELETE. The button element and its onClick stay unchanged.
CreateArea: import AddIcon and use <AddIcon /> in place of the text Add. Icons are SVG, so they scale cleanly, unlike a typed plus character.
Header.jsx: place <HighlightIcon /> inside the h1 next to the title text.

concepts.heading: Fab and Zoom
points: Replace the plain button with MUI's Fab (floating action button), a circular button with a built-in colour change on hover. Swap the tag only: <Fab onClick={submitNote}><AddIcon /></Fab>. Component names are capitalised, which is how JSX tells them apart from HTML tags.
Zoom is a transition wrapper. Wrap the Fab in <Zoom> and control it with the boolean in prop: true makes the child animate in, false hides it.
(Extra) Zoom requires a single child that can hold a ref; Fab qualifies.

concepts.heading: Challenge: expand the form on click (conditional rendering)
points: Desired behaviour: initially only a one-row textarea shows. Clicking it reveals the title input, grows the textarea to three rows and zooms in the Fab.
Add const [isExpanded, setExpanded] = useState(false).
Define expand() that calls setExpanded(true) and attach it as onClick on the textarea.
Render the title input only when expanded, using either a ternary with null or the && short-circuit form: {isExpanded && <input ... />}.
Make rows depend on state: rows={isExpanded ? 3 : 1}.
Pass the state to Zoom: <Zoom in={isExpanded}> instead of a fixed true.

concepts.heading: Background pattern
points: transparenttextures.com offers tileable transparent PNG patterns. The lecture picks one called cubes.
Copy the pattern's URL and add background-image: url(...) to the body rule in styles.css, keeping the solid background colour (#eee in the reference) so the translucent pattern shows over it.

concepts.heading: Persistence caveat
points: Refreshing the page loses all notes because React is only the front end and keeps state in browser memory.
Saving notes would need a backend and database, such as Node with MongoDB from earlier modules. (Extra) localStorage is a lightweight alternative for a client-only app.

task.name: Make the create-note form expand on click
task.starting_point: Keeper app with working add/delete, MUI installed, form className 'create-note', Fab wrapped in Zoom with in set to true, title input and 3-row textarea always visible.
task.goal: Show only a one-row textarea at first; on click, show the title input, make the textarea 3 rows and zoom in the Fab.
steps: Open CreateArea.jsx (form already has className="create-note", Fab wrapped in <Zoom in={true}>).
Add const [isExpanded, setExpanded] = useState(false) at the top of the component.
Write function expand() { setExpanded(true); } and attach it to the textarea with onClick={expand}.
Wrap the title input in {isExpanded && ( <input name="title" ... /> )} so it is only rendered after the click (a ternary returning null works too).
Change the textarea's rows attribute from the fixed "3" to rows={isExpanded ? 3 : 1}.
Change <Zoom in={true}> to <Zoom in={isExpanded}> so the Fab animates in only when the form expands.
In Header.jsx import HighlightIcon from @mui/icons-material/Highlight and render <HighlightIcon /> inside the h1 before the text.
In styles.css add background-image: url("https://www.transparenttextures.com/patterns/cubes.png") to the body rule.
Test: reload, confirm only one row shows, click it, type a title and note, click the yellow + button and confirm the note card appears with a delete icon.
task.expected_result: Page loads with a compact note box; clicking it expands the box with title field and animated yellow add button; adding a note still works.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.44 React Dependencies and Styling the Keeper App/using-pre-built-react-components/src

pitfalls: Forgetting the create-note className or updated stylesheet leaves a grey, mispositioned button.
Using the old @material-ui imports from the video with a modern React setup; use @mui/* paths.
Capitalisation: Fab not fab, otherwise React treats it as an unknown HTML element.
(Extra) The form never collapses again in this version: isExpanded only ever goes from false to true.

(Extra) MUI's Fab renders <button type="button">, so unlike a plain <button> inside a form it does not submit the form by itself; event.preventDefault() in submitNote is now just a safety net. Keep onClick={submitNote} on the Fab itself, not on Zoom.
Expecting notes to survive a refresh.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (playground files exist only for sections 1-11, 14, 15).
gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson 'Using a component library (MUI)'. Blurb: install pre-built React components, render icons as components, and drive a transition from state.

Tasks: (1) import DeleteIcon and render it inside the Note delete button; (2) replace the Add <button> with MUI <Fab> holding <AddIcon />; (3) wrap the Fab in <Zoom in={...}> and toggle it with a boolean; (4) add isExpanded state so the form starts as a one-row textarea; (5) render the title input with && and switch rows with a ternary.
Starter code: the finished Keeper add/delete app (App, CreateArea, Note, Header) with plain text buttons and form.create-note CSS already in place.

Demo idea: an isExpanded toggle beside the live form, with the JSX lines {isExpanded && ...}, rows={isExpanded ? 3 : 1} and in={isExpanded} highlighted as they flip between values, plus a side-by-side of plain <button> vs <Fab> rendering.

Infrastructure prerequisite: the playground vendors only Bootstrap and CodeMirror; MUI lessons would need React, ReactDOM, Babel standalone and an ESM/UMD build of @mui/material and @mui/icons-material (with Emotion) loaded in the preview frame.
